correctness.rationale: Lucas factorization is proved directly by binomial digit splitting and carry exclusion. The digit vector is verified exactly; the low-digit carry partitions give the seven explicit recurrence coefficients, valid under cyclic wrap. A complete induction with nonzero divisible shifts, interior shifts and two boundary cases proves both extremal values and uniqueness for every depth; four-sign moment inversion proves all pair counts. The standalone exact checker independently tests the original binomial sums and direct cyclic sums through bounded depths (3,098 assertions). Its finite scope is not used as proof of the infinite statements.

broader_coverage.reasoning: A broader general digital-carry framework can compute such correlations algorithmically, but finite cyclic wrap and the sharp all-shift extrema at each block size require specialized inequalities and equality classifications. The Delannoy and Apéry sign vectors differ. No inspected broad theorem yields these numeric sharp bounds and their precise extremizers as an immediate special case.

The present claim adds an exact finite cyclic recursion, two sharp and unique extremizer families valid at every depth, and all four pair-sign counts. It does not claim novelty for Lucas or for carry methods.

The result does not assert the methods or digital factorization are new. Residual risk is an implicit earlier specialization of a general transducer or character-correlation theory.

value.rationale: This is a natural complete all-shift problem for the first useful quadratic-character digit model of the classical Apéry sequence. The exact finite cyclic recurrence gives all two-sign joint counts, while the sharp extremum theorem identifies moving positive and fixed negative shift scales and unique extremizers for every block depth. Such equality classifications are not generic consequences of digit multiplicativity, and the result is a meaningful full finite-scale structural classification rather than an arbitrary numerical case.
